Tone/style: in a McKinsey one-pager style, crisp and assertive, no hedging.

q-data-narrative-number-reconciliation: The monthly performance review for Portfolio K indicates a generally controlled quarter with a few pressure points that deserve targeted follow-up before the next operating cycle. In October, total units sold were 1,832, which established the volume baseline used in the rest of this assessment. Pricing quality held up in November, where average revenue per unit reached $23.65, suggesting that discount leakage remained contained in that period. Service stability improved as the return rate fell by 140 basis points from September to October, a shift that points to better fulfillment discipline. At the aggregate level, Q3 total revenue came to $119,484, confirming that end-of-quarter demand carried the top line despite product-mix changes. Channel mix remains strategically material: April online order share was 48.2%, so digital demand now has direct implications for staffing and fulfillment cadence. Overall, the pattern supports focused intervention rather than broad alarm, because the core demand signal stayed stable while only a few execution levers moved significantly.
